title: What Does a 500 Sq Ft Minimum Mean for Refinishing One Room?
meta: A 500 sq ft refinishing minimum means a 300 sq ft Seattle bedroom bills at 500 × $3.99 = $1,995. Why minimums exist and how to use one, from Wills Flooring.
keywords: hardwood refinishing minimum charge, 500 sq ft minimum refinishing, cost to refinish one room hardwood, refinish one bedroom cost Seattle, minimum job size floor refinishing

blocks.lead: It means the job is billed as if it were 500 sq ft even when the room is smaller: a 300 sq ft Seattle bedroom refinished at the natural rate costs 500 × $3.99 = $1,995, not 300 × $3.99 = $1,197.
blocks.detail: Above 500 sq ft you pay only for the measured area. Stairs are priced per tread and sit outside the minimum. The smart move is to add a hallway or closet so you get 500 sq ft of actual floor for the money you are spending anyway.

blocks.html: The phone call usually goes like this: "I only need the one bedroom done, it is about 12 by 13, what would that be?" In Seattle that one room is often a Wallingford or Beacon Hill bedroom where the carpet came up and revealed oak, or a Capitol Hill condo where the previous owner's dog lived in one spot. The room is 156 sq ft. Our published rate is $3.99 per sq ft, so the caller expects around $620. The real answer is $1,995, and this post explains why that number is fair, why nearly every refinisher has one like it, and how to make sure you get full value from it.

blocks.text: Why every refinisher has a minimum

items.title: The setup is the same
items.text: A crew loads a drum sander, an edger, a buffer, vacuums, three grits of abrasive and finish, drives into Seattle, finds parking, and sets up containment. That takes the same two hours for 150 sq ft as for 900.

items.title: Cure time does not shrink
items.text: Three coats of Bona water-based finish need the same dry time between coats whether the room is a closet or a great room. A small room still ties up two to three days of the crew's calendar.

items.title: Materials have a floor
items.text: Sanding belts, edger discs, a sealer coat and finish come in fixed quantities. A partial can of finish left over from a small room is often wasted.

items.title: Warranty and insurance
items.text: We carry the same license, insurance and 1-year workmanship warranty on a $2,000 job as on a $10,000 job. The minimum is what makes small jobs possible at all rather than turned away.

blocks.text: How to use the minimum instead of eating it

items.html: Add the hallway. A Seattle upstairs hall is 60 to 100 sq ft and takes the most foot traffic in the house. It is almost always the best free addition.
Add the closets. Closet floors are included in the measured area if we sand them. Two reach-in closets add 20 to 30 sq ft and make the room look finished when the doors are open.
Add the room next door. Two bedrooms and a hall in a 1920s Ballard bungalow are typically 450 to 560 sq ft. You cross the minimum and pay only for real floor.

Recoat the adjacent rooms. If the living room finish is dull but intact, a screen and recoat at $1.99 makes the whole floor match the freshly sanded bedroom in sheen. This is the trick that avoids the "new room, old hall" look; see will one refinished room match the rest.
Do not count on stairs to fill it. Stairs are billed per tread, not by area, so 13 treads at $55 to $75 do not reduce the 500 sq ft floor minimum. They are a separate line.

blocks.text: One-room jobs that are still worth it

a.title: Pay the minimum when
items: The room has pet stains or water marks that make it unlivable as is
You are converting the room (nursery, home office) and want it done before furniture arrives
The rest of the house is carpet or tile, so there is nothing to match
It is a condo and the one room is your entire hardwood area
You plan to sell and the room photographs for the listing

b.title: Hold off when
items: Adjacent rooms will need refinishing within two years anyway; do them together and pay once
The floor only looks dull; a $995 recoat may be all it needs
The room is under 150 sq ft and could be covered by a rug you already own
You are also planning a kitchen remodel that will spill dust into that room

blocks.title: Seattle condos:
blocks.text: Most Capitol Hill, Queen Anne and Belltown condos have 400 to 700 sq ft of hardwood, so the minimum rarely bites. What does add cost is elevator reservations, loading-zone permits and quiet-hour restrictions. Tell us the building rules at the estimate and we build the schedule around them; none of it changes the per-square-foot rate.
Questions to ask any Seattle refinisher about their minimum

items.d: Is the minimum in square feet or dollars?
items.text: Ours is 500 sq ft, which converts to $1,995, $3,250 or $995 depending on the service. A dollar minimum with no area attached lets a company charge you for nothing.

items.d: Do closets, halls and landings count toward it?
items.text: Yes, at Wills Flooring, if we sand them. Ask, because some companies measure only the main rooms and bill the extras separately.
No. Stairs are per tread. Anyone who folds stairs into a square-foot minimum is guessing, and the guess is rarely in your favor.

items.d: What else is added on a small job?
items.text: Dust containment (+$250) is optional but smart in an occupied Seattle house. Appliance moves apply only in kitchens and laundry rooms.
items.note: Example: 224 sq ft bedroom, natural, with containment = $1,995 + $250 = $2,245

items.d: Will you measure it in writing?
items.text: We measure to the foot at the free estimate and write both the measured and billed area on the quote, so you can see exactly how much room you have to add before it costs more.

faq.q: How much does it cost to refinish one bedroom in Seattle?
faq.a: At Wills Flooring's published rates, any bedroom under 500 sq ft bills at the 500 sq ft minimum: $1,995 for a natural finish, $3,250 with stain, or $995 for a screen and recoat. Most Seattle bedrooms are 120 to 250 sq ft, so adding the hallway and closets costs nothing extra.

faq.q: Why is there a 500 sq ft minimum for refinishing hardwood floors?
faq.a: Setup, travel, equipment, three coats of finish and two to three days of dry time cost the same for a small room as for a large one. The minimum covers those fixed costs so a company can take small jobs at all. Nearly every professional refinisher has a minimum in either square feet or dollars.

faq.q: Do stairs count toward the 500 sq ft minimum?
faq.a: No. Stairs are priced per tread, $55 to $75 each at Wills Flooring, and are a separate line on the quote. A 200 sq ft room plus 13 stairs is billed as 500 sq ft of floor plus 13 treads, so 500 × $3.99 + 13 × $55 = $2,710 at the low end.

faq.q: Can I add another room later and avoid the minimum?
faq.a: Each visit is its own job with its own minimum. Refinishing a 200 sq ft bedroom now and a 200 sq ft bedroom next year costs $1,995 twice. Doing both plus the hall in one visit is typically 450 to 500 sq ft and costs $1,995 once. Grouping rooms is the single biggest saving.

faq.q: Does the minimum apply to a screen and recoat?
faq.a: Yes. A recoat has the same 500 sq ft minimum, which works out to $995. A recoat only works if the old finish is intact with no bare wood, and it is a good way to make adjacent rooms match a freshly sanded room in sheen.

faq.q: Is the minimum different for stained floors?
faq.a: The area minimum is the same 500 sq ft; only the rate changes. Sand, stain and finish is $6.50 per sq ft, so the smallest stained job is $3,250. Because stain adds a full extra process and a day of dry time, small stained rooms are where the minimum feels largest.
